lines.speaker: d
lines.text: A Navy warship came back from sea with claws stuck in its hull.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: The frigate U.S.S. Stine had lost its sonar, hidden in a rubber dome under the bow.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In dry dock, the rubber was slashed. Eight percent of it, cut open.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Inside nearly every cut, a curved hook. The kind that rings a squid's suckers.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Except these were bigger than any squid hook ever collected.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: A petty officer named Eye-ruh Carpenter found the first one. He dug into the rubber with his knife, and it looked to him like a claw.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: He said the longest gash ran four feet.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: A Navy biologist called it a squid, but would not rule out something unknown.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: One estimate put the animal at a hundred and fifty feet. That number was never proven.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: The animal was never found. Did a giant squid leave those claws, or something nobody has named?
